answer: Each probe round begins at dawn, when a verifier opens an inlet to an agent and asks it to solve a fresh micro-benchmark with a hard 900-millisecond wall-clock deadline; because the same request floods every clone simultaneously, one GPU time-sharing trick lets only one member finish in time. The verifier stamps each passing proof with a lantern hash tied to that deadline, then cross-checks timestamps against peer receipts. A clone caught past deadline gets its emissions frozen and its stake, roughly $40, slashed to zero.
